description: Java dev CALLS set (#177): call sites of spring-framework v7.1.0 drawn by sample_java_sites.py (seed 177) — 60 at random from the production sources and 5 per hard Java case from a targeted stratum — each traced to its targets by reading the code at the pinned commit, never from myceliums output. Not held out: the #177 resolver fixes were made while reading its misses, so its scores are development numbers (see java-spring-heldout.json for the held-out set). Reported per stratum and per case by graph-eval, never gated.
rules: Sites are drawn by sample_java_sites.py (seed 177) and read in the order of the draw. Strata: `random` takes the first 60 sites that qualify; each case stratum takes the first 5 that qualify and really are that case. A site is skipped when it is not a call made inside a named method or constructor (a declaration, an annotation, a string, a comment, a field initialiser, an abstract or interface method declaration), when it repeats a pair already taken, or, in a case stratum, when it is not that case (a static import of a library method, a field Spring does not inject, a type that is not an interface or abstract class). The caller is the innermost named method or constructor containing the call, including methods of anonymous classes and enum constant bodies; calls in lambdas belong to the enclosing method. A pair lists every project symbol the caller's calls of that name bind to under javac's rules: the declaration of the receiver's static type (inherited declarations where the class does not declare it; the overload javac selects) and, where the call dispatches, every override of it in the repository (found by git grep over the subtypes). `new X(...)` targets the class X and its matching constructor. An empty list means no call of that name in the caller binds to a project symbol: a JDK or library method, a method inherited from a library base class, an implicit member with no declaration (a record accessor). Annotation elements (`ann.value()`) are interface methods and are targets. Method references (`Type::m`) are labelled with what they reference but are not calls under the fixture rules: they are reported apart and left out of the totals. `inner-anonymous` is set mechanically: the caller's declaration is indented two levels or more (spring-framework indents with tabs).

cases.dispatch: the call goes through an interface or abstract (or overridden) method: the declaration the receiver's static type binds, plus every override in the repository
cases.overload: the callee name has several overloads in view; the target is the one javac picks (arity alone may not decide)
cases.generics: the receiver's type comes from a type argument (List<DataBuffer>.get(0)) or a type-parameter bound (C extends X)
cases.inner-anonymous: the caller is a method of a nested, inner, local or anonymous class (enum constant bodies included)
cases.lambda: the call is written inside a lambda body; it belongs to the enclosing method
cases.method-ref: a method reference (Type::m, this::m). Not a call under the fixture rules (invokedynamic), so these pairs are reported apart and left out of the totals
cases.static-import: a bare call bound by a static import of a project method (`import static org.springframework...`)
cases.injected-field: the receiver is a field Spring injects (@Autowired, @Resource, @Inject, @MockitoBean) or a constructor-injected field
cases.inherited-library: the class extends a library type and the call reaches a method inherited from it: no project target
